THE MECHANISM, so a reader need not re-derive it: the second loop's two seeds are TRANSPOSED, not merely recoloured. Ours emits the byte-offset induction seed `li r29,0` at +0x118 then the stored-zero seed `li r22,0` at +0x11c; the target emits the stored zero first (`addi r28,r23,0`, copying the zero `li r23,0` seeded at +0x114) and the induction seed second (`li r29,0`). Without the [0x118,0x120) transposition the recolor is provably INCONSISTENT -- our r29, defined at +0x118 and read at +0x124 `add r24,r31,r29` and +0x144, would have to map to the target's r28 at its definition and to r29 at its uses -- so the permutation is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. After it, `constant_dataflow_recolor` naming OUR r23 re-encodes our word to `addi r22,r23,0` (the target's ENCODING around our register), and the remaining 16 words are two disjoint callee-saved transpositions in the first loop (ours g28/g26 against g26/g28, ours g24/g25 against g25/g24) plus the second loop's own webs, all completed by copy_register_fields and machine-proven by verify_consistent_recolor with NO unproven_recolor_audit escape.
